description: Age-based additions to the standard deduction: the classic §63(f) over-65 addition and the new OBBBA §70103 $6,000 senior bonus with its MAGI phase-out.

cases.name: Single, age 67 — over-65 addition + senior bonus (full)
cases.citation: IRC §63(f)(1) ($2,000 Single TY2025); OBBBA §70103 ($6,000 bonus ≤ $75K MAGI)

cases.name: Single, age 67, $90K wages — senior bonus mid phase-out
cases.citation: OBBBA §70103(c) (phase-out linear over $30K window above $75K Single MAGI)

cases.name: Single, age 67, $120K wages — senior bonus fully phased out
MFJ, both 67, $100K wages — senior bonus ×2
cases.citation: OBBBA §70103(a) ('each taxpayer who has attained age 65'); IRC §63(f)(1)(B)
cases.rationale: Base 31500 + 2×1600 (both over-65) + 2×6000 (both senior bonus, MAGI ≤ $150K) = 46700. Engine only adds the $6,000 bonus once regardless of how many spouses are 65+.
hints: engine.mjs: look inside `compute1040` around the `if (age >= 65) { ... std += TY.seniorBonus; ... }` block
the senior-bonus branch should fire once for the taxpayer and once for the spouse when MFJ and both 65+
current code only checks `age` (taxpayer) and adds the bonus a single time

cases.name: MFJ, taxpayer 50 / spouse 68 — spouse qualifies for senior bonus
cases.citation: OBBBA §70103(a) (per qualifying individual, not per return)
cases.rationale: Base 31500 + 1600 (spouse over-65) + 6000 (spouse senior bonus, MAGI ≤ $150K) = 39100. Engine gates the entire senior-bonus block on `age >= 65` (taxpayer), so spouse-only over-65 never triggers the bonus.
hints: the guard `if (age >= 65) { ... std += TY.seniorBonus; ... }` should also fire when `spouse_age >= 65` on an MFJ return
consider extracting senior-bonus amount as `numSeniors * 6000` and running the phase-out on that

cases.name: MFJ, both 70, $200K wages — over-65 ×2, senior bonus fully phased out
cases.citation: IRC §63(f)(1)(B); OBBBA §70103(c) (phase-out ends at MAGI $180K MFJ)
